use: Casual 'it's fine' or 'it's good': mada ikeru (I can keep going), kore ikeru (this is tasty).
notes: Also just 'can go': ashita ikeru? (can you make it tomorrow?). Don't confuse with ikenai (mustn't).

use: Mostly as an exclamation, tsuiteru! (lucky!), or in the negative, tsuitenai (no luck).

example.romaji: Kyou wa honto ni tsuitenai na.
example.ja: 今日はほんとについてないな。
example.english: I've had no luck at all today.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou wa hontou ni tsuite imasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は本当についていませんね。
examplePolite.english: I've had no luck at all today.

notes: Same verb as tsuku (stick to), so it can also mean 'it's attached' or 'it's switched on'.

use: The goods are the subject: yoku ureru (sells well); also an entertainer making it big.

example.romaji: Kono hon, sugoku ureteru rashii yo.
example.ja: この本、すごく売れてるらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently this book is selling really well.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono hon wa sugoku urete iru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: この本はすごく売れているそうです。
examplePolite.english: Apparently this book is selling really well.

notes: uru is 'sell' (you sell it); ureru is 'it sells'.

use: Guessing an answer, winning a prize, or hitting a target.

example.romaji: Nani ga haitteru ka, atete mite.
example.ja: 何が入ってるか、当ててみて。

examplePolite.romaji: Nani ga haitte iru ka, atete mite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 何が入っているか、当ててみてください。

notes: ataru is 'it hits' or 'you win': kuji ga atatta (I won the draw). Also 'put against': te o ateru (put a hand on it).

english: do well; play an active part
use: Someone shining in their role: at work, on a team, in their field.

example.romaji: Kare, ima Amerika de katsuyaku shiteru n da tte.
example.ja: 彼、今アメリカで活躍してるんだって。
example.english: I hear he's doing really well in America now.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa ima Amerika de katsuyaku shite iru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は今アメリカで活躍しているそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear he's doing really well in America now.

notes: Said of people, not plans; for a plan working out, use umaku iku.

use: Covers both arguments and physical fights, between friends, couples or kids.

example.romaji: Kinou kare to kenka shita n da.
example.ja: 昨日彼とケンカしたんだ。
example.english: I had a fight with my boyfriend yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou kare to kenka shita n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日彼とケンカしたんです。
examplePolite.english: I had a fight with my boyfriend yesterday.

notes: Usually X to kenka suru (fight with X). kenka o uru: pick a fight.

english: argue; have a row; be in dispute
use: A drawn-out dispute inside a group, often over money, plans or who decides.

example.romaji: Okane no koto de oya to momete n da.
example.ja: お金のことで親ともめてるんだ。
example.english: I'm having a row with my parents about money.

examplePolite.romaji: Okane no koto de oya to momete iru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: お金のことで親ともめているんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm in a dispute with my parents about money.

use: Picking on someone weaker; between friends it can be playful teasing.

example.ja: あんまりいじめないでよ。
example.english: Stop picking on me so much.

examplePolite.ja: あまりいじめないでくださいよ。
examplePolite.english: Please don't pick on me so much.

notes: Noun: ijime (bullying), a big social issue in Japan.

use: Mostly teikou ga aru: you feel uneasy about doing something.

example.romaji: Hitomae de hanasu no wa chotto teikou aru na.
example.ja: 人前で話すのはちょっと抵抗あるな。
example.english: I'm not too keen on speaking in front of people.

examplePolite.romaji: Hitomae de hanasu no wa chotto teikou ga arimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 人前で話すのはちょっと抵抗があります。
examplePolite.english: I'm a little uneasy about speaking in front of people.

use: Aiming at a goal or a place: X o mezasu (aim to become or reach X).

example.ja: 医者を目指してるんだ。
example.english: I'm working towards becoming a doctor.

examplePolite.ja: 医者を目指しています。
examplePolite.english: I'm working towards becoming a doctor.

notes: Also for direction: choujou o mezasu (head for the summit).

use: A contest to decide who wins: a game, a bet, a moment of truth.

example.ja: じゃあ、じゃんけんで勝負しよう。
example.english: OK, let's settle it with rock-paper-scissors.

examplePolite.ja: では、じゃんけんで勝負しましょう。
examplePolite.english: Well then, let's settle it with rock-paper-scissors.

notes: shoubu suru: go head to head. koko ga shoubu: this is the moment that counts.

use: Steady effort over time toward a goal.

example.romaji: Kare wa sugoku doryoku shita n da yo.
example.ja: 彼はすごく努力したんだよ。
example.english: He worked really hard for it.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa sugoku doryoku shita n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼はすごく努力したんですよ。
examplePolite.english: He worked really hard for it.

notes: Also a noun: doryoku ga mukuwareta (the effort paid off). For a quick push, say ganbaru.

use: Testing something to see if it works or suits you.

example.ja: 新しいアプリ、試してみた？
example.english: Have you tried the new app?

examplePolite.romaji: Atarashii apuri wa tameshite mimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 新しいアプリは試してみましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you tried the new app?

notes: For 'try doing', -te miru is more common: tabete miru (try eating it).

english: take on (a challenge); have a go at
use: Taking on something hard or new: X ni chousen suru.

example.romaji: Kotoshi wa marason ni chousen suru n da.
example.ja: 今年はマラソンに挑戦するんだ。
example.english: This year I'm taking on a marathon.

examplePolite.romaji: Kotoshi wa marason ni chousen shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今年はマラソンに挑戦します。
examplePolite.english: This year I'm taking on a marathon.

notes: English 'challenge' meaning a problem is kadai; chousen is the attempt itself.

use: Pushing a plan, job or talks forward: shigoto o susumeru.

example.ja: じゃあ、このまま進めよう。
example.english: OK, let's carry on as we are.

examplePolite.ja: では、このまま進めましょう。
examplePolite.english: Well then, let's carry on as we are.

notes: Sounds the same as susumeru 'recommend' (勧める). susumu is 'it moves forward'.

use: Works both ways: mondai o kaiketsu suru (solve it), mondai ga kaiketsu suru (it gets solved).

example.romaji: Mondai wa mou kaiketsu shita yo.
example.ja: 問題はもう解決したよ。

examplePolite.ja: 問題はもう解決しました。
examplePolite.english: The problem has already been solved.

notes: sore ja kaiketsu ni naranai: that doesn't solve anything.

use: Gathering things into one: notes, luggage, a group, an idea.

example.ja: 荷物、もう全部まとめた？
example.english: Have you packed up all your things?

examplePolite.romaji: Nimotsu wa mou zenbu matomemashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 荷物はもう全部まとめましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you packed up all your things?

notes: hanashi o matomeru: wrap up a discussion. Noun: matome (summary).

english: take on; accept (a job or request)
use: Agreeing to take responsibility for a job or a favour.

example.romaji: Ii yo, sono shigoto hikiukeru yo.
example.ja: いいよ、その仕事引き受けるよ。
example.english: Sure, I'll take that job on.

examplePolite.ja: 分かりました、その仕事を引き受けます。
examplePolite.english: Understood, I'll take that job on.

notes: Polite set form: ohikiuke shimasu. To turn it down: kotowaru.
